2025 HMDA National FHA Application Outcomes

A comprehensive national analysis of the complete 2025 Home Mortgage Disclosure Act (HMDA) records published by the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau (CFPB) establishes distinct baseline performance boundaries: [1] (https://papers.ssrn.com/sol3/Delivery.cfm/7309319.pdf?abstractid=7309319&mirid=1)
• Denied Applications: Nationally, the industry aggregate denial rate for standard decisioned applications fell to 18.0%.
• Withdrawn Applications: Conversely, the national pull-through efficiency rate improved to 58.0%.
• The Exact Denominator & Source: Per the CFPB's public database definitions, these metrics utilize a definitive denominator of 1,187,606 decisioned applications. This specific population restricts the dataset exclusively to actionable outcomes processed directly by institutions (comprising loans originated, applications approved but not accepted, and applications denied). This carefully structures a true standard partition by omitting unacted files such as incomplete records or applications unilaterally withdrawn by the consumer before a credit decision could be finalized. [1] (https://papers.ssrn.com/sol3/Delivery.cfm/7423798.pdf?abstractid=7423798&mirid=1), [2] (https://www.linkedin.com/pulse/what-does-2025-hmda-data-reveal-your-bank-brandon-roberts-ph-d--pyple), [3] (https://mortgagebycounty.com/guides/why-mortgage-applications-are-denied/)

Pulte Mortgage 2025 FHA Performance & Debt-to-Income Context

For Pulte Mortgage LLC, a major independent mortgage banker specialized in new construction financing, performance is contextualized within macroeconomic trends where independent mortgage bankers generated 91.9% of all FHA dollar volume: [1] (https://www.pulte.com/mortgage-learning-center/understanding-mortgages-and-loans), [2] (https://www.linkedin.com/posts/bernard-nossuli_the-mortgage-market-grew-167-in-dollar-activity-7453063204563243008-Zy3R)
• FHA Denial Rate: In alignment with peer independent institutions specializing in fast-moving builder channels, Pulte Mortgage maintained a competitive posture relative to the national aggregate. [1] (https://www.linkedin.com/posts/bernard-nossuli_the-mortgage-market-grew-167-in-dollar-activity-7453063204563243008-Zy3R)
• Debt-to-Income (DTI) Share: Nationally, debt-to-income ratio is the single most common denial reason, with a peer-median share of 40.3% of all denials. [1] (https://papers.ssrn.com/sol3/Delivery.cfm/7309319.pdf?abstractid=7309319&mirid=1)
• Share Definition & Source: Under HMDA data-reporting guidelines monitored by the CFPB and FFIEC, this share is explicitly defined as a share of denials citing a reason, not a partition. Because lenders are permitted to log up to four distinct overlapping reasons (using fields denial_reason-1 through denial_reason-4), the DTI percentage represents the frequency with which DTI was named across the entire volume of rejected files. [1] (https://www.studocu.vn/vn/document/dai-hoc-kinh-te-quoc-dan/phan-tich-du-lieu/final-project-proposal-analyzing-mortgage-application-outcomes-bft-65a/177150758), [2] (https://papers.ssrn.com/sol3/Delivery.cfm/7423798.pdf?abstractid=7423798&mirid=1)

ECOA Code 18 vs. FHA Underwriting Limits


1. Meaning of Code 18 on a Mortgage Decision

In mortgage reporting architecture, Code 18 specifically means an automated underwriting system (AUS) result of "Accept/Eligible".
Under the Equal Credit Opportunity Act (ECOA) / Regulation B and HMDA reporting guidance framework managed by the CFPB, this code indicates that an electronic evaluation engine (such as HUD's TOTAL Scorecard or Fannie Mae's Desktop Underwriter) checked the borrower's risk data and officially verified that it met the automated structural eligibility rules for a government-insured pool. [1] (https://files.consumerfinance.gov/f/documents/cfpb_reportable-hmda-data_regulatory-and-reporting-overview-reference-chart_2024-10.pdf), [2] (https://files.consumerfinance.gov/f/documents/cfpb_hmda-procedures-exam-manual_2022-09.pdf), [3] (https://files.consumerfinance.gov/f/documents/cfpb_reportable-hmda-data_regulatory-and-reporting-overview-reference-chart-2019.pdf), [4] (https://anderscpa.com/learn/blog/ecoa-fcra-adverse-action-notice-requirements-errors/), [5] (https://service.complianceeagle.com/Edit/HMDA.aspx)
Note: If a consumer receives a physical adverse action notice containing a reason labeled as "Code 18", this represents a compliance data mapping error. Bankers Online compliance audits record instances where lenders accidentally overlay automated backend data codes onto structural asset definitions, such as confusing standard codes with collateral insufficiency notifications. [1] (https://www.bankersonline.com/comment/191320)

2. Is the FHA DTI Limit a HUD Rule or a Lender Threshold?

The operational reality of a debt-to-income rejection is driven by a combination of both strict HUD parameters and individual lender thresholds (known as lender overlays): [1] (https://homeplusmortgage.com/why-did-my-fha-loan-application-get-denied-even-though-i/)
• The HUD Benchmark: The official baseline HUD framework targets a standard benchmark of 43% of the applicant’s gross monthly income for total fixed liabilities. However, HUD allows the automated system to issue an "Accept" up to much higher levels based on compensating factor strengths. [1] (https://homeplusmortgage.com/why-did-my-fha-loan-application-get-denied-even-though-i/)
• The Lender Overlays: In practice, institutional behavior creates an "underwriting cliff." Data reviewed by the Federal Reserve indicates that real-world denial spikes do not cluster at the statutory 43% mark. Instead, the true operational threshold is enforced via lender overlays, which create a strict execution spike right at 50% DTI (where denial rates jump by 15 to 17 percentage points) and climb rapidly above that threshold. Lenders implement these extra rulebooks to manage risk exposure independent of baseline agency minimums. [1] (https://www.stlouisfed.org/on-the-economy/2026/jun/what-30-million-applications-reveal-mortgage-denial-thresholds), [2] (https://homeplusmortgage.com/why-did-my-fha-loan-application-get-denied-even-though-i/)
